posts.caption: TypeSafe AI launched Jev on Sept 15: a 'System One' model that returns typed choices, scores and yes/no answers with probabilities instead of text. $0.042 per million input tokens; output is free.
TypeSafe AI left stealth Sept 15 with a $40M seed led by DCVC. Founder and CEO Diogo Almeida is a former OpenAI researcher; Erik Gafni and Sasha Sheng are co-founders.
Vercel: Jev reached nearly 13% of paid AI Gateway teams in 24 hours, the fastest-adopted model in gateway history, 2x the GPT-5.6 family. Caveat: it was free on the gateway through Sept 25.
TypeSafe says Jev answers in 70-500 ms and was 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper than an average of GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 on its own workflow evals. No independent benchmark yet.
Browser Use open-sourced Jev Ultrafast (MIT): Jev picks the action and page element, a small LLM writes text only when typing is needed. A Zurich-London Google Flights search took 7.1 s.
Jev Ultrafast perf notes: the optimized loop cut median browser protocol calls from 1,092 to 101 and median task time by 25%. Browser Use flags it: three run pairs, not a broad benchmark.
Hassan (@nutlope) classified 1,018 AI papers into 24 topics with Jev for $0.08 total, 256 ms median latency per paper. Summarizing them first with DeepSeek V4 Flash cost $3.99.
TypeSafe's Jev docs: asking 13 questions about one document in a single call was 12.2x cheaper and 10x faster than 13 separate calls, with the same answers. State is billed once per call.
OpenAI DevDay added a Decisions API in limited preview: GPT-6 Luna answers user-defined questions with fixed answer sets to classify inputs, route requests or pick an action.
GPT-6.1 Sol is in the API, ChatGPT Work and Codex at $2/$10 per M tokens, cached input cut to $0.10/M. OpenAI: 75.2% on DeepSWE v1.1 vs GPT-6 Sol's 68.8%, at ~76% lower cost per task.
OpenAI's new Ultrafast tier for GPT-6 Astra: up to 8x faster token generation (300 tokens/s) in Codex and up to 6x in the API, paired with WebSocket mode. Ultrafast for GPT-6.1 Sol is coming.
OpenAI's Agents API is in public beta: the Codex agent harness, run on OpenAI's infrastructure, with OpenAI-hosted sandboxes or your own (E2B, Modal, Daytona, Vercel). No fee beyond tokens and tools.
GPT-6 Sol ($2/$10 per M tokens) and GPT-6 Luna ($0.10/$0.50) launched Sept 22, priced 50% below GPT-5.6 promo rates. Both are in the API, Codex and ChatGPT Work.
Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on Sept 22: $4/$20 per M tokens, cache reads $0.20/M, about 40% cheaper than Opus 5 on typical work and 30%+ faster output. 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0.
From Anthropic's Opus 5.5 notes: one early tester finished a 680,000-line code migration in under a day, and asked to cut load times across a web app, Opus 5.5 succeeded 39 of 40 times.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 is out: $2/$10 per M tokens, 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Sonnet 5: 10.3%), 30%+ faster output. Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 follows in the coming weeks.
Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are one model with different safeguards. Fable 5.1 is generally available; Anthropic estimates it costs ~25% less than Fable 5 thanks to cheaper cache reads.
Claude Code's /advisor lets the main model consult a stronger one, e.g. Opus 5.5 with Fable 5.1 as advisor. It sees the full session incl. tool calls; Claude decides when to ask.
Claude Code 2.1.287 adds Claude Mods, letting plugins change deeper behavior, plus 'You should know', a built-in side agent that flags things you or Claude might miss.
Anthropic's new life-sciences lab reports Claude found an unrecognized system in a jumbo phage: a reverse transcriptase with CRISPR-like DNA repeat arrays and an accessory protein. Function unknown.
Anthropic and HHMI Janelia opened a preview of the Model Hardware Standard: one driver spec so any agent can run lab gear like microscopes, liquid handlers and robot arms, reachable over MCP.
Janelia, Google Research and Cambridge published the first complete male fruit fly CNS connectome in Cell: 166,000+ neurons, 11,691 cell types, covering the brain plus the ventral nerve cord.
Comparing male and female fly connectomes, the MaleCNS team found 262 sex-specific and 114 sexually dimorphic cell types, about 4.8% of the central brain.
A day after MaleCNS went public, Georgia Tech student Evan Sinclair Smith wired the fly connectome into Minecraft; Doom and Mario 64 ports followed. Neuron-to-control mappings are hand-picked.
